annotations.text:
Post-game replay on a phone: four directions, one real moment.
Seed 7007, Mustard / Green / Plum, turn 10 of 11. Green solves it next turn: Peacock, Rope, Study.
The bar: one strip per category; every still-plausible card is a segment as wide as that seat's belief. Solid = proven by the floor. Red mark = the truth, which only the replay knows.
The bar, the board and the scrubber are the same parts in a different order in each direction, so mixing is fair game.

A · Scrubber. Time first: one moment, every seat side by side.
For: comparing the three methods at the same instant is the whole point.
Against: three seats fit a phone; six will need scrolling or thinner bars.

B · Case file. One seat, deep: its method, its evidence, its bar, its would-be accusation.
For: reads like the logbook, and has room for each method's own numbers (deals left, arms, plausibility).
Against: comparing seats means swiping between tabs.

C · Race. The whole game as one picture: who had placed what, when. The cursor drills into a turn.
For: the payoff in one glance, and it scales to six seats.
Against: abstract; the board is gone. Open question: what the y-axis is. Cards placed (drawn here) or belief in the true answer.

D · Table. Watch it again as a game: the board leads, the numbers follow, the suggestion is spoken.
For: closest to the feel of playing; table talk and the chat rail belong here.
Against: the belief detail is small; a merged strip per seat is all that fits.
